quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: When should you allow extra space between your vehicle and the car ahead?

options.text: When following a station wagon.
When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.
When following a small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles pulling trailers cannot see you if you drive directly behind them. Keep extra distance between you and these vehicles. Large vehicles also block your view of the road ahead, so extra space lets you see around them.

questions.question: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on water instead of touching the road. How can you prevent it in rain?

options.text: Use cruise control to keep a steady speed.
Decrease your speed.
Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.

questions.explanation: In rain, lower your speed to prevent hydroplaning. Driving too fast can cause your tires to ride up on water and lose contact with the road. This makes your vehicle very hard to control.

questions.question: You see heavy smoke covering the road ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Turn on your flashers and keep driving.
Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the road.
Turn on your high beams and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the right, and stop off the road.
questions.explanation: If you see heavy smoke ahead, slow down right away. Move as far right as you can and stop off the road. Check if it is safe before continuing. Some smoke can harm your eyes, lungs, or be dangerous in other ways.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet.
Tow-away zone.
Steep downgrade.
Roadwork ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell you about road conditions and hazards ahead. This sign warns you to drive carefully when the road is wet and slippery.

questions.question: When a small vehicle passes a large vehicle, the driver should be ready for:

options.text: Loud noises.
Extra air pollution.
Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
Falling vehicle parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind gusts from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles sideways. Drivers of small vehicles should be ready to steer carefully when passing large vehicles, especially at high speeds.

questions.question: You have a green light and there are pedestrians in the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: You must let them cross first.
You have the right to go first.
Pedestrians must wait for you to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must let them cross first.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians in the intersection. When turning on a green light, always let pedestrians finish crossing first.

questions.question: What is an important step when turning?

options.text: Check traffic in all directions.
Speed up.
Always move to the left lane.

questions.explanation: Before turning, look behind and to both sides of your vehicle to make sure it is safe. Adjust your speed to turn safely.

questions.question: What factors affect how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach
Your body weight
How much time passes between drinks
All three factors

questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Eating before or while drinking slows alcohol absorption, but it cannot prevent intoxication if you drink too much.

questions.question: What should you do if a tire blows out?

options.text: Release the gas pedal.
Do not brake right away.
Slowly reduce speed and pull to the side of the road.
Do all of the above.

questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, release the gas pedal and do not brake immediately. Slowly reduce your speed, gently apply the brakes, and pull off the side of the road.

questions.question: You see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane. What should you do?

options.text: The pedestrian must yield to you.
You must let them cross first.
Honk your horn to alert them.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must let them cross first.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means a person is blind or partially blind. You must always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians with a guide dog or white cane.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You must turn right.
Do not turn right.
You can turn right at a red light.

questions.explanation: This sign means no right turns are allowed. It is illegal to turn right at this intersection.

questions.question: A steady yellow light means the red light is coming. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, you should:

options.text: Stop.
Keep going and leave the intersection safely.
Speed up so you don't cause an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep going and leave the intersection safely.
questions.explanation: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, keep moving to get out of the intersection as fast as you safely can.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Talk to other drivers using signals and your horn.
Ignore what other drivers are doing.
Only drive on quiet side streets.
Avoid driving during busy times.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk to other drivers using signals and your horn.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do things that surprise other people. Let other drivers, cyclists, and walkers know what you are doing by using your turn signals when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use your horn when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill and see a heavy truck ahead of you. You should know:

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Large trucks often go slower than the speed limit, especially going uphill. Be careful when you come up behind a truck. When you cannot see far ahead on a hill, it is against the law to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines mean you can pass another vehicle from either direction.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no one can cross them to pass. Drivers going in either direction cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: Defensive driving is:

options.text: Spotting unsafe situations and acting to prevent accidents.
Passing bad drivers to stay ahead of them.
Staying very close to the car in front of you.
Quickly changing lanes through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting unsafe situations and acting to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you see dangerous situations and take action before an accident happens. It helps you avoid crashes caused by reckless, careless, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: Pass slowly.
Drive at the same speed as the car you are passing.
Pass quickly and safely.

questions.explanation: When you pass another car, do it fast to get back in your lane quickly. Return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the car you passed in your mirror.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Always dangerous.
Dangerous only if someone is helping you.
Only dangerous in big vehicles.

questions.explanation: Backing up is always risky because you cannot see well behind your vehicle. Always be extra careful when backing up.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in before turning left from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane closest to the left edge.
The lane closest to the center of the street.
The lane closest to the right edge.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left edge.
questions.explanation: To make any turn, use the lane that goes in the direction you want to turn. For a left turn from a one-way street, use the lane closest to the left edge.

questions.question: When turning left, you should not:

options.text: Signal to other drivers.
Cut the corner short.
Slow down.

questions.explanation: When turning left, slow down and signal at least 100 feet before the turn. Do not cut corners because this can interfere with other vehicles.
